absoluteDifficulty.audienceAndReasoningGround: This now tests recognition of the foundational PMEST framework in the classification of books and library knowledge, not technical notation. For readers regularly exposed to book publishing/cataloguing, five fundamental categories for facets and foci are an introductory organizing principle; those outside the theme can narrow to facet systems but cannot derive the exact PMEST set. It requires one conceptual association, not a specialist coding rule or multistep construction.

coupledAdjudication.finding: Current 88 (“ten main numerical classes”) also describes UDC ten main classes; proposed 88 now identifies DDC by its three-digit 800/900 Literature and History & geography labels.

Old broad facets/signs admitted both UDC and Colon Classification. Proposed UDC 90 asks the full common-sign set plus the language/form/place/time common-auxiliary set. Proposed Colon 91 now asks the system-wide five Fundamental Categories used to interpret each facet and focus (PMEST), an identifying conceptual doctrine rather than a shared colon sign or exact category punctuation mapping. UDC is still faceted/analytico-synthetic, but its official general auxiliary tables and facet descriptions do not use this five-category framework.
